# **B2B company discovery that starts with your business, not a filter.**

Your best-fit customers are rarely defined by industry, size and location alone.

A payments company may care about who receives money internationally.  
A retail software company may care about store count.  
A SaaS company may care about the tools a business uses.

That context is hard to fit into a few database filters.

So teams still spend hours researching companies, checking whether they actually fit, and finding the right people inside them.

Harvin was built to do that work.

**START WITH YOUR BUSINESS**

# **Tell Harvin what a good customer looks like.**

You already know more about your best customers than any database filter can capture.

Give Harvin that context once. It uses it every time it finds and researches companies for you.

### **What you sell**

What your product does, the problems it solves and who needs it.

### **Who already buys**

Add a few customers that converted and companies that didn’t.

### **Who you want to reach**

Tell Harvin the roles, functions and seniority you usually sell to.

### **What matters when judging fit**

Industry, geography, business model, technologies, locations, users or anything else important to your business.

**Harvin turns this into your Company Profile.**

From there, it knows what to look for — without asking you to rebuild the same filters every time.

**COMPANY DISCOVERY**

# **Discover companies that traditional databases can’t find**

Harvin uses your Company Profile to look beyond industry, employee count and revenue.

It searches for the things your best customers actually have in common — how they operate, what they sell, who they serve, the tools they use and the problems they may have.

That helps surface relevant companies your usual searches may not.

### **Search by what matters to your business**

**Business model**  
How the company makes money.

**Use case**  
Why the company may need what you sell.

**Customer type**  
Who they sell to or serve.

**Technology**  
The tools and systems they use.

**Geography**  
Where they operate, not just where they are headquartered.

**Company characteristics**  
Stores, locations, users, funding, revenue or other important criteria.

**RESEARCH & COMPANY FIT**

# **Find out which companies actually fit.**

Finding a company is only the first step.

Harvin researches the details that matter to your business, then shows how well each company matches what you are looking for.

### **Research what your targeting depends on**

**Business model**  
Understand how the company operates and makes money.

**Technology**  
See the tools and systems relevant to your offer.

**Locations or stores**  
Know the size of a physical business beyond employee count.

**Countries served**  
Understand where the company actually operates.

**Users, funding and revenue**  
Add the numbers that help you judge fit.

**Your own criteria**  
Ask Harvin to research other information important to your business.

### **See why every company fits**

Harvin brings that research together into Company Fit.

You see the score and the reasons behind it, so your team can decide which companies deserve attention.

**Harvin recommends. Your team decides.**

**Explore Research & Company Fit →**

**DECISION-MAKERS & CONTACTS**

# **Find the right people inside the right companies.**

Once Harvin knows which companies fit, it looks for the people most likely to buy.

You tell Harvin the roles, functions and seniority you care about. It searches for them in priority order and matches people by what their role actually means, not just by title keywords.

### **Find the right decision-makers**

**Role priority**  
CFO first. VP Finance next. Head of Payments after that.

**Function**  
Finance, Operations, IT, Security, Marketing or whatever matters to you.

**Seniority**  
Avoid people who are too junior for the conversation.

**Title meaning**  
Harvin understands that similar roles can have very different titles.

### **Then find their contact details**

Once the right person is matched, Harvin can find their:

**Work email**  
**Direct or mobile phone number**

Contact details are searched across multiple sources and charged only when found.

**Explore People Search →**

# **Your target companies keep changing. Harvin keeps up.**

New companies appear. Decision-makers change roles. Businesses expand. Priorities shift.

Harvin keeps checking the companies you care about and helps surface what changed, so your team is not working from an outdated list.

### **Stay on top of changes**

**New companies**  
See newly discovered companies that now fit your criteria.

**New decision-makers**  
Find relevant people who joined or moved into target roles.

**Fit changes**  
See when new information makes a company more or less relevant.

**Company changes**  
Track expansion, leadership moves, funding and other useful updates.

**Fresh contact data**  
Refresh emails and phone numbers when needed.
